Rule. Hold this rule for Estimates: Turn users and actions into QPS and bytes, within an order of magnitude. Say it before you pick a tool from System design.

Why it matters. Interviewers on the System design track listen for whether you can name the idea estimates and refuse the common wrong pick. The summary is the force: Turn users and actions into QPS and bytes, within an order of magnitude. If you cannot restate it, you will drift into product names or trivia.

SAMPLE example. SAMPLE: a prompt lands that fits Estimates. You restate the force in one sentence — Turn users and actions into QPS and bytes, within an order of magnitude. — then show a tiny walkthrough that would fail if you ignored that force. You label the SAMPLE answer with the cost or the tradeoff, not with a brand name.

When to use. Use Estimates when the prompt's access pattern or force matches the summary above, when a prior slug in its after-list is already in hand, and when saying the rule changes which next step you take.

When to refuse. Refuse Estimates when a simpler tool already covers the force, when a prerequisite in after is still missing, or when applying it would invent a mechanism the track never taught. Prefer naming the missing slug over bluffing.
